CLAUDE.md

Source: CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

What this is

fastsae is an R package (CRAN, GPL-3) for Small Area Estimation: frequentist EBLUP models in compiled C++ (RcppArmadillo, RcppEigen, OpenMP) and Bayesian hierarchical models via INLA or, optionally, NumPyro/JAX MCMC through reticulate. Its main selling points are speed and numerical agreement with reference packages: the EBLUPs agree with sae (and emdi) to rounding error where both use the same method, and the HB models are checked against exact posteriors, Stan and tipsae. Changes to estimators should keep that agreement, and the tests compare against those packages. The documented, deliberate differences from sae (boundary rho and ML information in the SFH MSE; constrained REML fallbacks) are listed in NEWS.md and the Rd files.

Commands

Run from the repo root (see also main.R):

Rscript -e 'Rcpp::compileAttributes()'          # after adding/renaming any // [[Rcpp::export]] in src/
Rscript -e 'devtools::document()'               # regenerate man/ from roxygen
Rscript -e 'devtools::test()'                   # full test suite
Rscript -e 'devtools::test(filter = "eblup_sfh")'   # single file: tests/testthat/test_eblup_sfh.R
Rscript -e 'devtools::check()'                  # R CMD check
R CMD INSTALL . --preclean                      # force a clean C++ rebuild
Rscript calc_cov.R                              # local coverage -> cov_res.rds (FLIBS path is Homebrew gcc 16 specific)
Rscript -e 'pkgdown::build_site()'              # site into docs/
  • Bayesian tests and examples need INLA, which is not on CRAN: install.packages("INLA", repos = c(getOption("repos"), INLA = "https://inla.r-inla-download.org/R/stable"), dep = TRUE). Without it, those tests are skipped (skip_if_not_installed("INLA")) and do not fail. The same goes for sae, emdi, sf, and MASS. The jax_engine() tests need Python with jax/numpyro (setup_numpyro_env()) and are skipped on CRAN and without it.
  • Scripts in benchmarks/, rjournal/ and the vignettes use the installed fastsae, not load_all(). Run R CMD INSTALL . --preclean before benchmarks or renders, or the numbers come from an old build (this happened once: the installed build was days older than the source).
  • pkgdown/index.md is the site home page and is written separately from README.Rmd; benchmarks/update_benchmark_docs.R writes the benchmark tables into both, and into vignettes/benchmarks.Rmd and vignettes/hb-area-inla.Rmd.
  • README.md is generated from README.Rmd. Edit the .Rmd and knit it.

Package plumbing gotchas

  • DESCRIPTION has an explicit Collate: field. A new R/*.R file must be added there or it won’t be loaded. Order matters: utils.R, inla_utils.R, RcppExports.R, and methods.R come before the model files.
  • NAMESPACE is maintained by hand. It has no roxygen “Generated by” header, so devtools::document() will not rewrite it. Add new export() and S3method() lines manually.
  • C++ functions are exported under dot-prefixed internal names via // [[Rcpp::export(.name)]]: .eblup_core, .seblup_core, .seblup_pbmse, .seblup_npbmse, .eblup_stfh_core, .pbmse_stfh, .eblup_twofold_core, .bhf_fit_cpp, .pbmse_bhf_cpp, .eblup_bhf_cpp. R/RcppExports.R and src/RcppExports.cpp are generated, so don’t edit them by hand.
  • src/Makevars uses C++17 + OpenMP + LAPACK/BLAS. Stale src/*.o / fastsae.so files are in the tree locally, so use --preclean when header changes don’t seem to take effect.
  • .Rbuildignore excludes benchmarks/, rjournal/, paper/, playground/, docs/, data-raw/, vignettes/articles/, main.R, calc_cov.R, and inst/extdata. Those directories are dev-only, and package code must not depend on them.
  • Roxygen markdown is not enabled package-wide: a block that uses backticks or *emphasis* needs @md, or they appear literally in the Rd.

Architecture

Two engines, one result class. Every model function returns a list with S3 class "fastsae" (plus subclasses: fastsae_unit, fastsae_hb_area, fastsae_hb, fastsae_hb_unit, fastsae_hb_twofold). The shared methods in R/methods.R (print, summary, coef, fitted, residuals, plot), as well as autoplot, compare_sae, benchmark_sae, diagnose, map_sae, and export_sae, all work on this common shape. They find estimates through .sae_table() in R/utils.R (df_hb %||% df_eblup), so a new model has to fill one of those data frames with the standard columns (domain, y, eblup|hb, vardir, mse, rse, ...), plus estcoef, formula, call, data, and model.

Frequentist path (eblup_*): the R wrapper parses the formula/vardir, builds X via model.matrix, calls a C++ core for REML/ML Fisher scoring and MSE, then adds metadata and does back-transformation in R. - eblup_fh → src/eblup_fh.cpp (supports transform = "log": conditional-mean back-transformation exp(mu + g1/2) and delta-method MSE done in R, not the full Slud–Maiti correction) - eblup_sfh (SAR spatial) → src/eblup_sfh_core.cpp, with the sparse Cholesky machinery in src/sar_engine.h (no D x D inverse); parametric and non-parametric bootstrap MSE live in eblup_sfh_pbmse.cpp / eblup_sfh_npbmse.cpp (OpenMP, header eblup_sfh.h) - eblup_stfh (spatio-temporal, Marhuenda et al.; REML only) → eblup_stfh_core.cpp (+ analytical MSE g1+g2+2g3-g4, block-structured, header eblup_stfh_core.h) and eblup_stfh_pbmse.cpp; it sorts the panel into domain-major order internally and predicts NA cells (unsampled domains, missing periods) - eblup_twofold (sub-area level model of Torabi & Rao, 2014; area means in df_area) → eblup_twofold.cpp - eblup_bhf (unit level) fits REML/ML in C++ (src/eblup_bhf_core.cpp, likelihood profiled in gamma = s2u/s2e) and predicts with src/eblup_unit.cpp; the bootstrap MSE is driven by .pbmse_unit() in R with replicates in C++ (.pbmse_bhf_cpp). lme4 is only in Suggests.

Bayesian path (hb_*): hb_area (6 likelihood families; spatial iid/besag/bym/bym2/leroux/sar/slm; temporal rw1/rw2/ar1; Knorr-Held space-time interactions), hb_unit and hb_twofold (Gaussian/binomial/Poisson) take an engine object from R/engine.R: inla_engine() (default; builds INLA formulas and calls INLA::inla) or jax_engine() (NumPyro NUTS via reticulate; R side in R/hb_*_jax.R and R/python_env.R, Python in inst/python/hb_area_numpyro.py). Both engines share the default priors (half-normal sd(y) for Gaussian SDs, half-normal(1) on the link scale otherwise; see vignettes/hb-priors.Rmd). The helpers in R/inla_utils.R handle the INLA install check, converting a weight matrix into an INLA graph, and pulling posteriors out into df_hb. Gaussian models (and Leroux/SLM) use INLA’s classic mode, others compact. The old method = "laplace" lme4 route is removed (deprecated argument forwards to inla_engine()). hb_area temporarily sets INLA to single-threaded mode and restores the setting on exit.

Benchmarking comes in two forms. Don’t mix them up: - Self-benchmarking (self_benchmark = TRUE argument on the model functions): .setup_self_benchmark() in R/utils.R augments the data and formula before fitting, and .compute_benchmark_summary() reports the calibration afterwards. - Post-hoc benchmarking (benchmark_sae() in R/benchmark.R; the benchmark() alias was removed) adjusts a fitted object and returns class fastsae_benchmark.

Supporting modules: create_weights / spatial_test (spatial weights from sf polygons, Moran/LM tests), gvf_smooth (generalized variance function smoothing of vardir), step_sae (stepwise covariate selection), compare_sae (Bland-Altman/CCC agreement, no Pearson r), add_reliability_flags (BPS RSE tiers 25%/50%), and sim_area_data / sim_series_data (simulation generators; sim_spatial_weights is internal). Example datasets live in data/ (mys, mys_proxmat, mys_panel, sim_area, sim_panel, cornsoybean*) and are documented in R/data.R.

Tests

testthat edition 3, one file per module in tests/testthat/. Coverage is close to 100% (test_coverage_gaps.R exists specifically to hit edge branches), so new branches need tests. helper-simulate_safe_sfh.R generates well-identified SFH data on a row-standardized grid. Use it instead of mys_proxmat subsets for SFH bootstrap tests, because those subsets push rho to ±1 and make the SVD fail. Some code comments and dev notes (playground/, test helpers, main.R) are written in Indonesian.

Non-package directories

  • benchmarks/: speed and accuracy scripts against sae, emdi, and tipsae. bench_frequentist.R (with bench_frequentist_child.R) times fastsae, sae and emdi on the same data, each cell in its own process with peak RSS; validation/agreement_reference.R checks agreement with sae/emdi; sim_mc_finite_pop_d500.R is the design-based simulation; validation/ also holds the prior and INLA-mode studies. Outputs go to inst/extdata/*.rds (read by the vignettes and the article) and benchmarks/output/. After re-running, Rscript benchmarks/update_benchmark_docs.R refreshes the tables in README, the site home and the vignettes.
  • rjournal/: the R Journal article (fastsae.Rmd, fastsae.bib, README_RJOURNAL.md with the build steps and which script feeds which table). Verify every new reference (Crossref/DOI) before adding it: earlier versions of the bib and Rd files had wrong DOIs and non-existent references.
  • paper/: old LaTeX build files only.
  • playground/: standalone INLA tutorials, not part of the package.
